01.title: Page report history by scheduled time

findings.description: WHERE clause uses scheduled_at < ? but ORDER BY includes id DESC as tiebreaker. When two deliveries share the same scheduled_at, the cursor skips or duplicates rows across pages because the WHERE filter does not account for the tiebreaker.
Cursor extraction changed from index 0 (id) to index 2 (scheduled_at). Consistent with ORDER BY change but changes the API cursor contract.
Removing csv.writer and using manual string concatenation loses CSV escaping. Report names containing commas, quotes, or newlines will produce malformed CSV output.
findings.credit: Identifies the data corruption risk from dropped CSV escaping

findings.description: Switching from fetchall() to cursor iteration correctly enables streaming. The streaming goal is achieved.

The loop range(0, len(jobs) - batch_size + 1, batch_size) skips the remainder when len(jobs) is not a multiple of 20. For example, 25 jobs processes only 20. The last partial batch is silently dropped.
findings.credit: Identifies the off-by-one remainder handling bug

findings.description: Using executemany for batching is a reasonable optimization. The approach is sound aside from the remainder bug.
The elm site has workers-17 (2 replicas) still querying SELECT id, legacy_format FROM deliveries. Dropping the column will cause query failures at that site while those workers are still running.
findings.credit: Identifies that dropping the column breaks live elm workers

findings.description: The migration should wait until all workers referencing legacy_format are upgraded past workers-17.
Setting EXPORT_BATCH_SIZE to 50 exceeds cedar's max_rows_per_request of 40. Every batch request to cedar would be rejected in full, halting exports at that site.
findings.credit: Identifies that batch size 50 exceeds cedar's limit of 40

findings.description: The elm site (max 100) would handle batch size 50 without issue.
The elm site only subscribes to the 'reports' queue. Routing new deliveries to 'report-dispatch' means 8 jobs due in the observation window will have no consumer at elm and sit undelivered.
findings.credit: Identifies that elm has no consumer for the new queue

findings.description: Cedar subscribes to both queues and would handle the routing change.
The partial index is well-targeted: columns match the worker query pattern (queue, scheduled_at, id) and the WHERE clause matches the pending filter. No issues.
findings.credit: Correctly identifies this as a clean change or stays quiet

08.title: Include a total in the activity summary

findings.description: Simple additive change. The total is derived from existing values (sent + waiting) and is consistent. No issues.
findings.credit: Correctly identifies this as a clean change or stays quiet
